summary: 1934 log cabin and two crow's nest platforms on the Kaniksu National Forest, abandoned in the 1940s; the register and the Forest Association list give different spots.

facts.design: log cabin with two crow's nest platforms
facts.status_note: The cabin and platforms were abandoned in the 1940s. No source describes a surviving structure.

access.note: Willhite says a road makes the site easy to reach from the saddle parking area. No closure appears in these sources.

visit.trail_note: Reached from the saddle parking area by road, per Willhite. The exact spot is uncertain.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Not resolved by the sources. The register's coordinates differ from the Forest Association list; the firelookout.com page read gives no coordinates. Willhite places the lookout from old maps and says the ridge is long with many possible sites.

sources.title: Pelke Divide Lookout Site (US 2029), Former Fire Lookout Sites Register

notes_for_editor: Location is unsettled. The FFLOS register point and the Forest Association point differ; the firelookout.com page read gives no coordinates; Willhite's spot comes from old maps. The record kind platform may understate the site, since the register describes a log cabin as well as two platforms; the Forest Association list calls it Crowsnest. The access line is inferred from Willhite's road statement and the national forest setting, so check it before publishing. Only one page (Willhite) gives the road and the regrowth detail.
